label: rejected

evidence.V1: Three-quarter reads as a log via the ringed end; front and silhouette are a featureless bent capsule that could be a stick or pipe.
evidence.V2: Big trunk and tiny stub only; end rings give some small detail but there is no medium level (no bark plates, knots or broken end).
evidence.V3: Essentially a slightly bent octagonal cylinder with a peg-like stub; stiff primitive proportions.
evidence.V4: Soft long bark ridges versus a hard-edged, separate-looking end-grain disc; bevels inconsistent.
evidence.V5: End-grain close-up: the round ring cap does not follow the faceted bark outline, leaving bark corners protruding past the disc; minor stray faceting along the bark.
evidence.V6: Bark brown in 2-3 values plus cream rings - disciplined; birch/redwood colourways swap cleanly.
evidence.V7: 672 tris vs medium target 2000 - well under target.
evidence.V8: Vertex-colour material and bark palette match, but the stub reads as a cream peg and the end cap looks pasted on rather than a fused shell.
evidence.V9: Static scenery flags correct (Anchored, Hull, CanTouch off, Color white, bottom-centre origin).

evidence.V1: Reads as a log with a branch stub in front, top, three-quarter and silhouette views.
evidence.V2: Big trunk, medium end grain and branch stub, small bark ridges - clear tiers.
evidence.V3: Gentle bend and slight taper help, but it is essentially a long uniform tube with a tiny stub; little stylised exaggeration (no swelling, broken end or root flare).
evidence.V4: Bark ridges are softly rounded, but the end-grain face meets the bark at a hard faceted polygon edge with no rim chamfer (end_grain close-up).
evidence.V5: End-grain close-up shows a visible polygonal outline on the round end and faceted ridge kinks along the silhouette; bark shading otherwise clean.
evidence.V6: Bark brown in two values plus cream end-grain/stub cap; colourways consistent (birch rings get low contrast).
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, smooth fused organic shell, bark hue + cream end grain - consistent with nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; stub seated on log.

evidence.V1: Reads as a log from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette: long bent cylinder with a branch stub breaking the outline.
evidence.V2: Big log body and ringed end grain read, but medium/small tier is thin: one stub, no bark grooves, knots or split cap detail on the second end.
evidence.V3: Gentle bend and taper help, but the body is still a fairly uniform octagonal tube; partly exaggerated, not a confident stylised log.
evidence.V4: End-grain rim has a clean chamfered lip that catches light, but the bark ridges are hard long facets and the far end reads as a jagged polygon in the three-quarter view.
evidence.V5: Bark gradients are clean, but the end_grain studio close-up shows a small dark notch where the bark shell meets the cap at the upper right; minor.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: bark brown in 2-3 values plus cream end-grain rings; colourways (birch, redwood) keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 672 tris vs medium target 2000, well under.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, smooth shaded wood hue with cream secondary, chamfered cap rim; fits the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, white MeshPart colour, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; gates A1-A18 pass.

artifacts: End-grain disc outline mismatched with faceted bark silhouette
Stub branch cap reads as a separate cream peg (penetration 0.43 into log)
Polygonal outline visible on the end-grain cap
Hard unchamfered edge where the end grain meets the bark
small dark notch/crease at bark-to-end-cap junction (end_grain studio close-up, upper right)
far end cap outline reads jagged/polygonal in three-quarter view
top_fixes: Add medium forms: bark plates/ridges, a knot, and a broken or tapered branch instead of the peg stub
Make the end cap follow the bark profile with a chamfered rim
Exaggerate the bend/taper so the silhouette reads as a log from the front
Add a rolled bark lip / chamfer around the end-grain caps and a few more segments so the round end does not read polygonal
Push stylisation: slight mid swelling, an uneven broken far end or a second stub
Raise end-grain ring contrast in the birch colourway
Add a second tier of detail: bark grooves or a couple of knots plus a second smaller stub or broken branch
Increase segment count or soften bark ridges so the ends read round, and fix the cap junction notch
Push the silhouette more (stronger taper toward one end, slight flare at the root end)
